lines.text: My devotion,--

lines.text: As it were, to ride day and night; and not to deliberate, not to

lines.text: remember, not to have patience to shift me,--

lines.text: My knight, I will inflame thy noble liver,

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: God save thy grace, King Hal; my royal Hal!

lines.text: The heavens thee guard and keep, most royal imp of fame!

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: God save thee, my sweet boy!

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: My lord chief-justice, speak to that vain man.

lines.speaker: Lord Chief Justice
lines.text: Have you your wits? know you what 'tis you speak?

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: My king! my Jove! I speak to thee, my heart!

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: I know thee not, old man:  fall to thy prayers;

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: How ill white hairs become a fool and jester!

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: I have long dream'd of such a kind of man,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: So surfeit-swell'd, so old, and so profane;

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: But, being awaked, I do despise my dream.

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Make less thy body hence, and more thy grace;

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Leave gormandizing; know the grave doth gape

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: For thee thrice wider than for other men.

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Reply not to me with a fool-born jest:

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Presume not that I am the thing I was;

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: For God doth know, so shall the world perceive,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: That I have turn'd away my former self;

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: So will I those that kept me company.

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: When thou dost hear I am as I have been,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Approach me, and thou shalt be as thou wast,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: The tutor and the feeder of my riots:

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Till then, I banish thee, on pain of death,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: As I have done the rest of my misleaders,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: That lack of means enforce you not to evils:

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: And, as we hear you do reform yourselves,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: We will, according to your strengths and qualities,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Give you advancement. Be it your charge, my lord,

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: To see perform'd the tenour of our word.

lines.speaker: King Henry IV
lines.text: Set on.

lines.text: Master Shallow, I owe you a thousand pounds.

lines.text: Yea, marry, Sir John; which I beseech you to let me have

lines.text: That can hardly be, Master Shallow. Do not you grieve at this;

lines.text: I shall be sent for in private to him:  look you, he must seem

lines.text: Sir, I will be as good as my word:  this that you heard was

lines.text: but a colour.

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Fear no colours:  go with me to dinner:  come, Lieutenant

lines.speaker: Sir John Falstaff
lines.text: Pistol; come, Bardolph:  I shall be sent for soon at night.

lines.text: I like this fair proceeding of the king's:

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: First my fear; then my courtesy; last my speech. My fear is, your

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: displeasure; my courtesy, my duty; and my speech, to beg your

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: pardons.  If you look for a good speech now, you undo me:  for

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: what I have to say is of mine own making; and what indeed I

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: should say will, I doubt, prove mine own marring. But to the

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: urpose, and so to the venture.  Be it known to you, as it is very

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: well, I was lately here in the end of a displeasing play, to pray

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: your patience for it and to promise you a better. I meant indeed to

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: pay you with this; which, if like an ill venture it come unluckily

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: home, I break, and you, my gentle creditors, lose. Here I promised

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: you I would be and here I commit my body to your mercies:  bate me

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: some and I will pay you some and, as most debtors do, promise you

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: infinitely.

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: If my tongue cannot entreat you to acquit me, will you command me to

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: use my legs? and yet that were but light payment, to dance out of

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: your debt. But a good conscience will make any possible satisfaction,

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: and so would I. All the gentlewomen here have forgiven me:  if the

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: gentlemen will not, then the gentlemen do not agree with the

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: gentlewomen, which was never seen before in such an assembly.

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: One word more, I beseech you. If you be not too much cloy'd with fat

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: meat, our humble author will continue the story, with Sir John in it,

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: and make you merry with fair Katharine of France:  where, for any

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: thing I know, Falstaff shall die of a sweat, unless already a' be

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: killed with your hard opinions; for Oldcastle died a martyr, and this

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: is not the man.

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: My tongue is weary; when my legs are too, I will bid you good night:

lines.speaker: Epilogue (a Dancer)
lines.text: and so kneel down before you; but, indeed, to pray for the queen.
